_comment: Hand-maintained facts that are not in a data file. Keep in step with Chapter 5 and Figure 4.5 of the report. 'components' = the data-to-backtest steps that produced the reported results; 'capabilities' = each MLOps/DataOps capability, the AWS service in the design and the local equivalent that actually ran. Everything else is read from the report tables, reports/ and git.

latest_dag_run.result: All 23 tasks succeeded or were skipped by a branch
details: Closed loop, normal run (scheduled__2026-11-22): paper trading updated, monitor reported the champion healthy, the DAG took the skip_retrain branch; the whole run succeeded

Retrain smoke test (shown above): retrain forced with a tiny training budget (4,096 steps) and promotion disabled; 3 challengers trained one at a time, all failed the quality gate, champion v5 kept, 'Retrain failed the quality gate' email received in Mailpit
A full-size drill (3 x 300,000 steps) was stopped after 45 minutes: four trainings in parallel oversubscribed the CPU (DEF-15) and one task hit an MLflow experiment-creation race (DEF-14); both fixed
Evidence: reports/live/evidence/2026-11-23/ (task states, task logs, email list)
latest_dag_run.note: The smoke-test challengers were deliberately undertrained, so their gate failure shows the wiring works, not that retraining cannot produce a better model.

limitations: One held-out test period (414 trading days, December 2024 to July 2026) dominated by two weather-driven price spikes, so each result depends heavily on a few days.

Paper trading (simulated) covers only 96 trading days since 7 July 2026 in a flat gas market; the champion is 3 percentage points ahead of Buy & Hold, too short and too small a gap to call it reliably better. The champion was chosen on 23 November using validation data only (to December 2024).
Trading is simulated at each day's published spot price with a fixed 0.1 % transaction cost, without bid-ask spreads or market impact.
The reward does not penalise risk, and the agents accepted drawdowns of up to 53 %.
The main configuration was trained with five seeds and no hyperparameter search; full-test returns ranged from +67.0 % to +190.9 %.
The system has not been used for real trading, and none of the results supports acting on its decisions without a human trader reviewing them.

capabilities.local: Airflow 2.8.1 in Docker Compose: daily schedule, retries and a 2-hour timeout; the pipeline and the closed loop (paper trade, monitor, retrain branch, gate, promote, alerts) ran end to end (TC-14)
S3 API through LocalStack: raw data, processed splits, data-quality and backtest reports written by the DAG
transform.py run as the DAG's transform task
8 validation rules stop a bad run; the data_quality_report task stores a report for every run
MLflow 3.14 server in Docker for DAG runs, and the mlruns/ store behind every result in Chapter 5

MLflow Model Registry (file store in mlruns/): a 3-check quality gate on validation data decides which models are registered as energy_trading_ppo; the approved model carries the alias champion. Applied retroactively to the 5 fixed-reward seeds: all passed; seed 4 (v5) is champion

Paper trading (simulated) on new EIA data, monitoring and a champion/challenger retrain branch in the DAG; retraining is unit-tested end to end and ran in Docker as a smoke test, but no full-size retrain has replaced the champion
Airflow emails on success and failure (TC-17) and closed-loop alerts (retrain required, champion replaced, retrain failed the gate, champion kept), received in Mailpit
Champion health after every paper-trading update (return gap vs Buy & Hold, 60-day gap, drawdown from peak) with thresholds in drl.yaml; Airflow task logs; metrics in MLflow
Airflow image built from Dockerfile.airflow by Docker Compose, with the library versions used for the reported models
102 automated tests (pytest, with moto standing in for S3) pass
Fixed seeds, YAML config and a fixed data snapshot; re-evaluation reproduced the logged results exactly (TC-09)
